raw_answer_text:
A1: The `clk` signal toggles at a constant, regular rate throughout (shown as a repeating "p" pattern), independent of req/ack/done.

A2: At the start, req, ack, and done are all resting low.

A3: The request signal transitions (asserts) first; ack asserts only after req has already gone high.

A4: No — in the diagram, ack only rises to high after req has already risen and remained high for some time; there is no point where ack is high while req is still low.

A5: Req returns to low only after ack has asserted (gone high) and remained high for a period, consistent with req dropping in response to the acknowledge.

A6: Ack returns to low only after req has already dropped back to low, consistent with ack dropping in response to req's de-assertion.

A7: Done marks completion of the handshake; it asserts at the same time req falls back to low (while ack is still high), and then falls low shortly after ack itself has fallen.

A8: (1) req asserts (0→1); (2) ack asserts (0→1); (3) req deasserts (1→0); (4) ack deasserts (1→0).
